sections.hypothesis: Holding whichever of BTC and ETH rose more over the last 90 days, and cash when neither rose, gives a better risk-adjusted return than holding BTC or ETH alone.
sections.rationale: Dual momentum (Antonacci) combines relative strength with an absolute filter and has a long record across asset classes; for crypto only informal backtests were found, no rigorous study. The appeal is low turnover and the cash rule, which should sidestep long bear markets as trend-vol-target does. Weak points: two highly correlated assets give little to choose between; ETH lagged BTC for much of 2022-25; and a single 90-day lookback is one point on a curve. Lowest prior of the five. Context: after 139+ trials every bet against the trend has failed, cross-sectional momentum over small coins failed (-92% drawdown), and the one strategy marked Pursue is trend-vol-target on BTC daily (Sharpe 1.21 vs 1.07 for holding on the current config, but +639% vs +1,420% return). This note is one of five momentum ideas tested together on 2026-11-13; five ideas at once are five or more trials, so a single pass is weaker evidence than it looks.
sections.rules: Daily bars; runs on the coin universe but reads and holds only BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT. Every Sunday's close (UTC): each coin's return over the last 90 days; the higher one is held fully if positive, otherwise cash. Cash until both have 90 days of history. Decide at the close, trade at the next open; 2% no-trade band; long only, spot; 10 bps fee, square-root impact; spread 1 bp for single-coin runs, by the coin's volume band for universe runs. Every strategy starts cold at the first month: cash until its lookbacks fill, the same convention as every earlier test.
sections.falsification: UNIVERSE 1d, 2020-01 to 2025-10, defaults, 330 USDT, run once. Reject unless all hold: (1) Sharpe above BTC buy-and-hold's (the run's benchmark, 1.07 on this window) and above ETH buy-and-hold's (1.12, from run 20261113-073756-eb5043's benchmark); (2) max drawdown no worse than BTC buy-and-hold's; (3) total return beats BTC held at the strategy's average exposure; (4) break-even cost at least twice the cost paid.
sections.costs: Weekly decisions; a switch only when the leader changes or the market turns: perhaps 5-15 round trips a year at about 22 bps.

history.reason: Pre-registered test (UNIVERSE 1d, 2020-01..2025-10, lookback 90; run 20261113-075830-087aa2). Failed rules 1 and 2: Sharpe 1.06 vs 1.07 for BTC and 1.12 for ETH buy-and-hold; drawdown -76.9% vs -76.6% for BTC. Passed 3 and 4: +1,334% against +727% for BTC at the same 68% exposure; break-even 665 bps vs 22.
